Title: Tidal Routing: Load-Aware Expert Selection for Mixture-of-Experts Inference

Authors: Camille Moreau, Yusuf Haddad, Maja Lindqvist
Abstract: Mixture-of-experts models route each token to a few experts, but in batched inference the chosen experts are often unevenly loaded, so a handful of busy devices set the pace for the whole step. We present Tidal Routing, a drop-in change to the router that adds a small, load-dependent penalty to each expert's score at inference time, without retraining. The penalty is computed from queue lengths that the serving system already tracks, and it is bounded so that no token is sent to an expert outside its original top-$2k$ candidates. On three open models with 8 to 64 experts, Tidal Routing reduces p99 step latency by 18 to 31 percent, and it changes downstream accuracy by less than 0.3 points on every benchmark we tested. We release our scheduler patch and the traces used in all experiments.
